name: Hobgoblin Fleshcarver

alignment.name: Evil
alignment.description:
Evil creatures don’t necessarily go out of their way to hurt people, but they’re perfectly willing to take advantage of the weakness of others to acquire what they want.
	Evil creatures use rules and order to maximize personal gain. They don’t care whether laws hurt other people. They support institutional structures that give them power, even if that power comes at the expense of others’ freedom. Slavery and rigid caste structures are not only acceptable but desirable to evil creatures, as long as they are in a position to benefit from them.

items.name: Glaive
items.description: With its long, wooden haft that ends in a swordlike cutting blade, the glaive excels at keeping enemies at a distance.

description: This is the size of a typical human and serves as a standard in the game. This category has no special rules.

traits.name: Fleshcarver's Trap
traits.details: each enemy that starts its turn within the aura takes 5 damage the first time it moves during that turn.

traits.name: Phalanx Soldier
traits.details: A hobgoblin fleshcarver gains a +2 bonus to AC while at least one hobgoblin ally is adjacent to it.

auras.name: Fleshcarver's Trap
auras.details: each enemy that starts its turn within the aura takes 5 damage the first time it moves during that turn.

hit.description: poison damage, and the target is slowed (save ends). If the target was already slowed, it is instead immobilized (save ends)

powers.name: Defensive Dart
powers.trigger: when the hobgoblin fleshcarver is hit by an enemy's melee attack

effect.description: The fleshcarver shifts 2 squares and uses toxic dart against the triggering enemy.

hit.description: damage, and the hobgoblin fleshcarver slides the target 2 squares. The target must end the slide within 3 squares of the fleshcarver

powers.name: Hobgoblin Resilience
powers.trigger: when the hobgoblin fleshcarver becomes subject to an effect

effect.description: The fleshcarver rolls a saving throw against the triggering effect.
